newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate passes major budget bill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate passes major budget bill.

text.p: The Australian Senate on Wednesday agreed to one of the larger contentious budget bills, delivering the government its first major parliamentary victory in its campaign to push through its fiscal tightening.
However, the Senate slightly watered down the Higher Education Amendment bill from its original form, in which it would have saved A$296 million next fiscal year, from July.
The bill contained two main fiscal measures:
-- Increased charges for some university courses, raising A$66 million in 1997/98.
-- A lower income threshhold initiating repayments of student debts to the tax office, raising A$230 million in 1997/98.
A spokesman for Education Minister Amanda Vanstone was unable to give a single-year estimate of the cost of the amendments, which would ease the burden on former students trying to support a family.
But he said that over the next four fiscal years the cost would be about A$60 million, compared to the bill's value of A$1.13 billion in that time.
All non-government parties opposed the bill but it passed with the Senate's two Independents supplying the two votes that the government needed.
In its August budget the government announced measures to cut the 1997/98 budget by A$7.2 billion.
More than a quarter of that, about A$2 billion, has been in doubt because of opposition in the Senate, the upper house of parliament.
Passage of this bill leaves about A$1.7 billion in doubtful bills.
In general, the government will need the uncertain support of the Independents for the passage of those remaining bills.
